course.title: Git — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: Learn Git from first principles through everyday commits, history inspection, branching and merging, remote collaboration, recovery, releases, internals, security and professional automation.
course.version_scope: Command behavior references checked against official Git documentation on 2026-10-15; current online reference pages surfaced Git 2.56 documentation. Re-check the installed version with git --version. Some flags and advanced repository features vary by Git version and by connected IDE/hosting platform. Git LFS is a separate extension.
prerequisites: Basic file and folder operations. A terminal is helpful but commands are introduced gradually. A repository you own or are authorized to use is needed for remote collaboration practice; never use production credentials or valuable repositories for destructive demonstrations.
learning_outcomes: Initialize or clone repositories and explain the working tree, index, references and commit object model.
Track, stage, review and commit focused changes; inspect history and compare repository states.
Create and maintain branches, resolve conflicts, synchronize remotes and contribute through code review.
Select safe recovery, merge/rebase, tag/release and backup strategies based on repository state and collaboration requirements.
Explain core Git security boundaries, advanced repository features and version-dependent limitations.
Build a reproducible team workflow and automation checklist with safe defaults and explicit verification.
